security_audit.summary: All 135 static alerts are false positives involving documentation, Go syntax, mocks, or explicit test operations. A separate integration fixture exposes weakly authenticated PostgreSQL and unauthenticated Redis through unrestricted host port bindings. No evidence found of malicious intent, credential exfiltration, or security-review prompt injection.

remediation.issue: The Docker Compose fixture publishes PostgreSQL and Redis ports without a loopback restriction or adequate authentication.
remediation.suggestion: Bind published ports to 127.0.0.1 or remove host publishing. Use generated test credentials and Redis authentication when network access is necessary.

semantic_findings.title: Test Services Exposed Through Unrestricted Host Ports
semantic_findings.description: The fixture publishes PostgreSQL as "5433:5432" and Redis as "6380:6379" without loopback bindings. PostgreSQL uses test/test credentials, and Redis has no configured authentication. Reachable hosts could access or alter fixture data when these examples run.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both published port mappings omit a host address, and the service configuration shows weak or absent authentication. Actual remote reachability depends on host networking and firewalls.

content.value_statement: Go test suites can miss edge cases, leak goroutines, and fail unpredictably. This skill guides test design, review, and debugging with concrete Go testing patterns.
actual_capabilities: Guide named table-driven subtests, public API assertions, test file organization, and correct testify assertion scope.
Design HTTP handler tests with request fixtures, response recorders, headers, and status assertions.
Demonstrate consumer-defined interfaces, testify mocks, reusable fixtures, and build-tagged database integration suites.
Recommend race detection, goleak checks, parallel test isolation, and deterministic time testing.
Show fuzz targets with seed inputs, executable examples, and size-parameterized allocation benchmarks.
Review test suites for coverage gaps, brittle assertions, shared state, and flaky timing.
limitations: This is instructional material, not a standalone test runner or a guarantee of correct generated tests.
Running examples requires Go and project dependencies; scaffolding uses gotests, and container fixtures require Docker Compose.
Version-specific API claims require verification against your installed Go release and module target.
Container examples need network hardening, and detailed CI workflows and benchmark methodology depend on separate referenced skills.

use_cases.title: Add Unit Coverage
use_cases.description: Create named subtests for public functions, boundary inputs, and error paths without coupling tests to private fields.

use_cases.title: Review Test Reliability
use_cases.description: Inspect pull request tests for assertion scope errors, shared mutable state, timing dependencies, and missing race checks.

use_cases.title: Organize Integration Testing
use_cases.description: Plan build-tagged database suites with fixture setup, per-test cleanup, and isolated test services.

prompt_templates.title: Write Your First Table-Driven Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Write named table-driven tests for [function]. Cover normal inputs, empty inputs, boundary cases, and documented errors. Assert observable results.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: add focused unit tests for an existing function.

prompt_templates.title: Test an HTTP Handler
prompt_templates.prompt: Test [handler] using request and response recorders. Cover valid requests, malformed bodies, missing authentication, and validation errors. Assert status, headers, and response content.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: test request handling without starting a network server.

prompt_templates.title: Debug Concurrent Test Failures
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate flaky tests in [package]. Check shared state, goroutine cleanup, assertion scope, and timing dependencies. Propose deterministic tests and race detection commands.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: diagnose intermittent failures in concurrent Go code.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Large Test Suite
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [repository] for unit coverage gaps, integration isolation, and goroutine risks. Separate findings by concern. Prioritize fixes with evidence and focused tests. Require disposable databases and loopback-only services.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: coordinate a test-suite review across multiple packages.

output_examples.input: Review tests that report every price subtest as passing even when the parent fails.
output: Finding: the assertion helper captures the parent test instead of the current subtest.
Correction: create the assertion helper inside each subtest.
Verification: deliberately break one expected result and confirm that the matching subtest reports failure.

output_examples.input: Plan tests for a PostgreSQL order repository without affecting normal unit tests.
output: Separate database tests with an integration build tag.
Start a disposable fixture, load the schema, reset records between tests, and close connections during teardown.
Bind fixture ports to loopback and keep production credentials out of the test environment.
Cover creation, missing records, user filtering, and database errors.

output_examples.input: Improve tests for a worker pool that may leak goroutines.
output: Add package-level goroutine leak checks and verify shutdown after queued work completes.
Coordinate workers with explicit synchronization instead of arbitrary delays.
Run concurrent access tests with race detection and keep each test independently runnable.

best_practices: Assert public behavior with named cases, including boundary inputs and failure paths.
Use disposable fixtures, loopback-only services, and explicit cleanup for integration tests.
Match examples to your Go version and run focused tests before expanding coverage.
anti_patterns: Treating a high coverage percentage as proof that assertions are correct.
Sharing mutable fixtures, relying on execution order, or using arbitrary sleeps for synchronization.
Running destructive fixture cleanup against shared databases or exposing test services to untrusted networks.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The declared supported tools are Codex and Claude Code. The guidance targets Go projects.

faq.question: Does the skill run tests by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides instructions and examples that an assistant can apply using your project tools and execution permissions.

faq.question: Which dependencies are required?
faq.answer: Go is required for execution, and gotests supports scaffolding. Testify, goleak, clockwork, and Docker Compose are needed only for relevant examples.

faq.question: Can integration tests stay separate from unit tests?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill recommends integration build tags and separate test commands, with fixture setup and cleanup.

faq.question: Will the examples work with every Go version?
faq.answer: No. Check version-specific APIs against your installed compiler and module target before adopting an example.

faq.question: Are the container fixtures secure without changes?
faq.answer: No. Restrict published ports to loopback or remove them. Replace weak credentials and enable authentication when services need network access.
